sentences.text: Bruntonichthys is an extinct genus containing only one species of arthrodire placoderm.
The skull of this animal measured approximately 139 millimetres in length and possessed eye sockets that were disproportionately large.
Experts suggest it likely hunted small mollusks.
Remains of this creature have been discovered in the Gogo Formation within the Kimberley region of Australia.
It is classified as a basal member of the clade Aspinothoracidi, which falls under the major group Pachyosteomorphi within Eubrachythoraci.
This fish lived during the Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian, between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago.
